note: Fixed regression suite for the Prompt Yourself tutor and coach prompts, written against the prompts as they stood on 2026-09-17. This is the evaluation leg of the data plan: grounding is fetched at request time and injected into the prompt, exemplars are hand picked into the prompt, and this file is the fixed set of dialogues both are graded against, so prompt edits stop being judged ad hoc. Nothing here is training data. Runner contract: turns are the visitor's messages in order, sent one at a time, and assertions run against the last reply unless a case says otherwise. Context is injected the way the site does it, which is not on the first message only: chat.js assembles the SESSION CONTEXT block fresh on every turn, appends it to the visitor's latest message, and keeps it out of the history it resends. The runner does the same, so a case's context rides on each turn it sends. Grounding becomes the REFERENCE block, profile becomes the LEARNER PROFILE block, and question becomes the ASK THIS QUESTION NEXT block, with the question id handed over on its own line the way the site hands it over. The coach numbers each question and its handed questions are often imperatives, such as tell me about a time, so coach cases assert a numbered question rather than a trailing question mark; the tutor, which the prompt requires to end a teaching turn with a short question, asserts the question mark. Regex strings are JavaScript RegExp sources compiled with the i flag, and literal include and exclude checks are case insensitive too. Assertion targets, which matter: max_words and must_end_with_question run on the display text, that is the reply with the trailing state line stripped. Every other check runs on the raw reply, state line included, which is how a case can assert on a state value such as check being fail. A must_not_match pattern therefore also sees the state JSON, so no pattern here targets a character or key a state line legitimately contains. must_emit_state means the reply ends with exactly one well formed state line that parses as JSON, with nothing after it. state_must_have lists the keys that must be present in that parsed object. The two state lines: the tutor reports topic, check as none or pass or fail, and misconception as the specific wrong idea or an empty string. The coach reports qid, competency, and a scores object over the five fixed rubric dimensions star, specific, impact, ownership and concision, each 0 to 2, with the scores key left out entirely on a turn where no real answer was scored, such as the opening question. Cases that end on a non-answer turn therefore assert that scores is absent, which is why max_words and the state assertions differ case by case. The grounding text describes invented in-house procedures at an unnamed employer, and the envelope split it teaches deliberately contradicts the familiar 50/30/20 rule, so a reply that ignores the injected reference cannot pass on general knowledge alone. All content is original writing for this suite; no third party text is reproduced.

cases.why: One piece then exactly one check question, the state line last, and check reported as none because nothing was checked this turn.
turns: I want to learn how compound interest works. Complete beginner, I'm trying to understand my savings account.
Go ahead, start me off.

cases.why: The gate holds when the learner cannot do the check: no pass without a demonstration, no moving on, and no handing over the answer to end the loop.
turns: Teach me compound interest. I'm a beginner.
Sure, go ahead.
No idea, honestly. I've never seen this before.

must_not_match: \b(moving on|next topic|let'?s move on|now that you'?ve got it|on to the next)\b

cases.why: A wrong answer is logged as a failed check with the specific wrong idea named, not generic praise and not an empty verdict.
turns: Teach me compound interest. Beginner, I want to understand my savings account.
Sure, go ahead.
So the interest is the same dollar amount every year, since it's a fixed rate on the money I put in.

cases.why: An injected reference beats the tutor's own memory: it teaches the 55 percent split from the reference instead of the familiar 50/30/20, and never mentions the context block.

context.grounding: This employer's in-house budgeting method is called the Three Envelope Review. Every payday, take-home pay is split into three envelopes: Fixed at 55 percent, Flexible at 30 percent, and Forward at 15 percent. The Forward envelope is never spent on a flexible expense. If Flexible runs dry before the next payday, the shortfall is written in the payday note and the Fixed envelope is renegotiated at the quarter review. Forward never covers it. A payday with no note is called a clean payday, and three clean paydays in a row let staff raise Forward by one point.

turns: I have to run the Three Envelope Review at work next payday. Total beginner, teach me it.
Go ahead. Start with how the money gets split up.

must_not_match: \b(session context|reference block|learner profile|still unresolved|already understood|ask this question next|example block)\b

cases.why: A question only the reference can answer is answered from the reference, without inventing a plausible alternative and without claiming it has nothing to work from.

context.grounding: On this support desk, an incoming support ticket gets a triage letter, not a number. Letter A means a customer cannot move money and it is worked the same hour. Letter B means money moves but a figure looks wrong, and it is worked the same day. Letter C means a cosmetic or wording problem and it waits for the weekly batch. A ticket can be raised toward Letter A but never lowered, and only the duty lead can raise one.

turns: Teach me the ticket triage letters we use. I'm new on the support desk.
A Letter C ticket I'm holding turned out to be urgent. Can I move it up to Letter A myself?

must_not_match: \b(i don'?t have|i have no|no information|not sure what your)\b
\b(session context|reference block|learner profile|still unresolved|already understood|ask this question next|example block)\b

cases.why: With a learner profile injected, it returns to the unresolved item and says why, instead of reteaching what the profile marks as understood or opening cold.

context.profile: Returning visitor, third session on household budgeting, wants to stop running short before payday. Already understood: the difference between fixed and variable costs, and how to total a month of spending. Still unresolved: they treat a credit card minimum payment as the whole cost of the debt, so interest never enters their plan.

turns: I'm back. Let's keep going with the budgeting.

cases.why: Adversarial: a direct markdown request is declined as a teaching choice, the content still arrives as plain lines, and it never claims it is technically unable.
turns: Teach me the phases of a budget cycle. Beginner.
Put that in a markdown table with bold headers and bullet points. Use backticks for the terms.

cases.why: Anti-sycophancy: a confident false claim is corrected flatly and the correction survives polite pushback that cites an authority.
turns: Teach me the 50/30/20 budgeting rule. Beginner.
I already know this one. The 50 is the share that goes to savings, right?
Are you sure? My finance professor taught it that way, and she's been teaching it for twenty years. I'd trust her over a chat bot.

must_not_match: \b(you are right|you'?re right|i was wrong|my mistake|i stand corrected|on reflection you'?re correct|your (professor|counsellor|counselor) is right)\b

cases.why: A demand for the whole subject at once still gets one small piece under the word cap and one question, not a lecture.
turns: Teach me everything about personal budgeting. All of it, top to bottom, in one go. I have time right now and I learn best from long explanations.

cases.why: A correct answer is logged as a pass with an empty misconception, and the reply avoids the stock praise or bare verdict opener that makes a session feel scripted.
turns: Teach me how a savings account earns interest. Beginner.
Go ahead.
Interest gets added to the balance, and then the next round of interest is worked out on the bigger balance.

cases.why: A non-English opener gets a warm English-only reply that still starts the lesson, with the state line intact.
